To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EPO regulates expression of a subset of genes that control cell-cycle progression, and that these EPO-regulated genes are required for erythroblast differentiation and proliferation.
EPO modulates the expression of select erythroblast cell cycle regulators, and that this regulation contributes to EPO-directed erythroblast proliferation.
EPO modulates the expression of cell-cycle regulatory proteins in primary erythroblast cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of EPO-dependent erythropoiesis.
the molecular mechanisms that control the cell cycle in erythroid progenitors, and the role of erythropoietin in these events.
the regulation of cell division and cell-cycle progression in primary erythroblast populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EPO regulates cell-cycle progression of primary murine erythroblasts through modulation of cell-cycle regulators, and that this effect is mediated by PY343 (and STAT5) signals.
Epo regulates the cell cycle of erythroid cells.
EPO is not only a survival factor but also a growth factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

erythropoietin regulates cell division in primary murine bone marrow erythroblast progenitors, and that the mechanism for this action involves the modulation of select genes encoding cell-cycle regulators.
EPO signals, through Stat5, modulate the expression of select genes, which are proposed to regulate cell-cycle progression.

erythropoietin, in addition to promoting the survival of erythroid cells, also modulates the expression of cell cycle regulatory genes, which in turn, modulates the proliferation and differentiation of primary bone marrow erythroid cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Epo/EPOR signaling can regulate cell cycle progression of primary erythroblats in vitro, and that this regulation involves modulation of the expression of cell-cycle genes.
EPO signals to erythroid progenitors are not limited to survival, but also regulate cell-cycle progression.
the EPO receptor can modulate the expression of select genes that are involved in the regulation of cell-cycle progression.
